questions.prompt: Where is Gold 1 carrying the puck?
questions.explanation: Gold 1 is drawn close to the puck-side boards in the defending half of the rink.

questions.prompt: Which two relationships fit the stated angling goal?

options.text: An approach that gives Gold 1 the middle for free
A route that permits recovery toward the Navy net

questions.explanation: The objective is to influence space while preserving recovery, not simply to arrive first.

questions.prompt: Order one angling read from this freeze.

options.text: Notice Gold 1’s route and your net
Update when Gold 1 passes or changes direction

questions.explanation: The approach changes with the carrier; this is not a fixed collision route.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into an example inside position beside the half wall.
questions.explanation: This reference stays inside Gold 1 and closer to the defending net. Several approach angles may satisfy the same relationship.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 passes inside to Gold 2. What deserves attention now?

options.text: Remain beside the wall and ignore the pass
Recover toward the new puck threat

questions.explanation: A release changes the threat. Retaining recovery momentum helps the next defensive action.

questions.prompt: Why can a fast approach be unhelpful if it sends you past Gold 1?
questions.explanation: Explain how overshooting may leave the middle or recovery route available to the attacker.

questions.prompt: Which teammate can support behind YOU if Gold 1 turns inside?
questions.explanation: D1 is positioned deeper behind YOU and can support recovery if Gold 1 turns inside; if D1 is pulled away, protect the route back to Navy’s net yourself.

questions.prompt: Which two conditions support an inside angle?

options.text: YOU can stay between carrier and net

questions.explanation: Inside position protects the net and D1 provides recovery support; skating past loses both control and angle.

questions.prompt: Move YOU closer to the inside lane beside Gold 1’s path.
questions.explanation: The inside spot keeps the carrier outside and preserves a recovery route to Navy’s net; if Gold 1 passes inside, switch threats.

questions.prompt: Why is the wall the preferred direction in this angle, while still requiring a read?
questions.explanation: Guiding a carrier toward the wall protects the middle, but the carrier’s speed, pass and support can change the next route; if Gold 2 appears inside, recover.

scenarios.title: Cover the lane after an interception
scenarios.objective: Change from an attacking pass intention to the nearest defensive cover after Gold intercepts
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. YOU attempted a pass in Gold’s zone; Gold 1 intercepted and Gold 2 moves through the middle. D1 is behind the play.
cues: Gold 2 is the second attacker moving middle; D1 is behind.

questions.prompt: Which two concerns follow the interception?

Calling updates teammates; taking nearer lane prevents a free attack; handoff keeps coverage connected.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a cover point that keeps Gold 1’s puck side and Gold 2’s middle route in view.
questions.explanation: This central point keeps the carrier side and middle support in view during the interception; if Gold 1 turns inside, follow the nearer threat and communicate the switch.

questions.prompt: Imagine D1 wins the puck back while Gold 2 remains in the middle. Which call gives the team useful new information?

options.text: D1 has it; Gold 2 is still middle
Keep the original forward passing pattern
Gold 2 is no longer a concern

questions.explanation: The call identifies D1 as the new carrier and Gold 2 as the remaining pressure cue. That updates teammates after the interception without promising a clear outlet. D1 still checks the lane before passing; YOU offer support that fits the new pressure.

questions.prompt: Name one attacking intention you must abandon after the interception.
questions.explanation: The planned forward pass is no longer the job once Gold owns puck, so call turnover and cover nearest lane; if Navy recovers, rebuild from new location.
